- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to match mean reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 3–5 days to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates near-term upside; cap forecast growth at 2–3% above recent 7-day moving average.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.8) and price is volatile, model tends to lag behind true trend; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment-weighted smoothing to forecast.
- In low-sentiment environments, model often underestimates downside risk; add 0.5–1.5% buffer below forecast for 3–5 day horizon to account for volatility.
- If model forecast is >+10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 2–4% if sentiment is weak or neutral; this prevents overconfidence in bullish signals.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates mean reversion; apply 1–3% downward adjustment if sentiment is weak or price has recently broken above 30-day MA.
